notes:
CRM notes (shorthand) - contact center automation lead; focus: agent-assist + resilient routing during spikes.
- Background: mid-sized CCaaS provider with retail & telco customers. Primary pain: seasonal spikes (holiday / product launches) produce queue backpressure, agents see stalled tool-calls.
- POC summary (week 1): Redwood Dedicated two-node pool for agent-assist and ticket summarization. Avg latency acceptable (~120ms per inference); observed p99 spikes to 900-1,100ms under synthetic burst tests (10k concurrent UI sessions).
- Requirements emphasized on call: "we need deterministic degradation strategy — if capacity hits limits, fallback to smaller model and queued summarization, not a total outage" (Head of Ops). Need automatic fallback routing by policy + regional failover.
- Important: tool-calling reliability (CRM & ticket system webhooks) during bursts — retries/backpressure handling required. Want function-calling with idempotency and tight timeouts.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + SSO/SAML required; data residency: US-only for certain retail customers; KMS/HSM for keys; audit logs preserved for 2 years. Legal flagged vendor clauses for on-prem offering.
- Redwood recommended config: autoscaling with pre-warmed capacity for predictable peaks, prefix/KV cache for repeating prompts (ticket templates), model variants (8B quantized fallback) and canary A/B rollout for new prompt templates. SE suggested Optimize recommendations for batching thresholds and cache TTLs.
- POC issues: first POC run failed p99 requirement (target p99 <600ms). Engineering wants to re-run with: (a) larger pre-warmed dedicated pool, (b) conservative batching limits, (c) enable prefix caching. Security wants KMS integration diagram before next exec review.
- Quotes / snippets: "If 30% of agents are waiting >1s the business impact is immediate — refunds and SLA credits" — Head of Customer Ops.
- Risk profile: High urgency (Black Friday simulation planned March 22). Procurement expects final cost estimate by 2026-03-25.
- Recommended next actions (internal): schedule KMS architecture review with Diego + Security; plan 48h engineered stress run at 10k concurrent sessions w/ logging to S3; prepare legal SOW with on-prem liability carveouts.
